spots.note: 15:32 afternoon run. Cam clear, bright full daylight, water readable edge to edge. Surface is wind-torn by the 18g23kt N cross-shore - heavy texture everywhere, waves breaking well outside as short crumbling sections that never stand up as a green wall; the whitewater is patchy and sectiony rather than one long peeling line. Scanned takeoff zone, both shoulders and the inside in all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames: no bodies, no boards, no paddling lines. Confident 0 out. One person leaning on the promenade wall at the right edge of the frame, but the cam is framed on the water so land count not applicable

15:32 afternoon run. Water fully legible, no glare, no blowout. The bay is very weak: thin reform lines sliding in towards the rock point with almost no height and no face ahead of the foam, plus uniform wind ripple across the whole bay. Nothing stands up in any of the 3 detail frames or the 6 sheet frames. Scanned the open bay, the corner by the rocks and the shorebreak in every frame: nobody in the water. 0 out, and with this little wave that is expected rather than a wasted lineup. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

15:32 afternoon run - cam UP again (second good run in a row after the sunrise 404). Sunny, deep blue, good visibility. Still the only working spot: waist-high lines breaking along the reef with a green face ahead of the foam in several frames, held up by the 18g23kt N blowing offshore here, but distinctly bumpier than the 11:31 run - 23kt gusts are putting chatter on the faces. Count is approximate: a scattered line of roughly 8 dark specks sitting out the back on the outside line, consistent across the +0s and +12s sheet frames, plus 3-4 resolvable in the crowd crops inside that same zone (higher of the two frames). Heavy wind chop makes an exact count impossible so 8 is a floor-ish read, not a precise figure. On land roughly 25: about 6 along the promenade railing and 15-20 sitting or walking on the sand. 8 out is right on the 8.0 average for this slot

15:32 afternoon run, wide distant cam so all counts approximate. Cam clean and bright. Wave is closing out badly: a continuous wall of whitewater across the whole beach dumping straight onto the sand, wind-chopped by the 18g23kt N cross-shore, no bank holding any shape - matches the VERY_POOR rating. Opened the detail crop and scanned the whole waterline in all 3 frames plus both crowd frames: no boards, nobody sitting outside the whitewater. Two dark specks standing in the shorebreak shallows near the lifeguard flag are bathers, not surfers, so 0 surfing rather than null. On land roughly 30: scattered groups and tents along the sand, a beach-volleyball style cluster at the right by the promenade, a few walking

11:31 lunch run. Cam clear, full daylight, no glare. Tide near the 11:08 low so the reef shelf is half dry - large areas of exposed rock and drained pools across the whole inside. What swell there is breaks well outside as short weak crumbly lines over the shallow shelf, chopped by the 18g21kt N cross-shore; nothing stands up as a green wall. Scanned takeoff zone, both shoulders and the inside channel in all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames: no bodies, no boards, no paddling lines anywhere in the water. Confident 0 out - the reef is simply not surfable at this tide and size. One person walking on the dry rock shelf. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

11:31 lunch run. Water fully readable, bright and legible edge to edge, no blowout. The bay is effectively flat: uniform wind ripple with only a thin wash breaking on the exposed rocks along the right-hand side, and reef showing through the shallows. No swell line stands up anywhere in the 3 detail frames or the 6 sheet frames. Scanned the open bay, the corner by the rocks and the shorebreak in every frame: nobody in the water. 0 out, and given how flat it is that is expected rather than a wasted lineup. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

11:31 lunch run - CAM IS BACK UP after being 404/dead at the 09:10 sunrise run. Sunny, deep blue water, excellent visibility. Best spot by a distance: clean waist-high lines peeling right along the reef with an unbroken green face ahead of the foam in several frames, held up and groomed by the 18kt N wind blowing offshore here. Counted in the crowd crops (higher of the two frames): a cluster of roughly 6-7 sitting/paddling in the left third plus 3 further out towards the middle peak, so 10 in the water; a couple more ambiguous specks not counted. On land 2 people standing out on the rock shelf in the crowd crops, plus roughly 10 more on the sand and along the promenade railing in the contact sheet - about 12 total, approximate. 10 out is below the 16.7 average for this slot

11:31 lunch run, wide distant cam so land counts approximate. Cam clean and bright, no glare. Wave is closing out: a continuous wall of whitewater running the length of the beach and dumping straight onto the sand, wind-chopped by the 18g21kt N cross-shore, no bank holding any shape - this reads worse than the POOR rating and matches the VERY_POOR it drops to from 15:00. Opened the detail crop and scanned the whole waterline in all 3 frames plus both crowd frames: no boards and nobody sitting outside the whitewater. A few dark specks are standing in the shorebreak inside the lifeguard-flagged zone - bathers, not surfers - so 0 surfing rather than null. On land roughly 20: a scatter of sitting groups and two tents along the top of the sand, a few walking, plus a handful by the rocks at the far end

08:56 sunrise run (task ran late). Cam clear, full daylight, water dark blue and legible edge to edge, no glare. Wave is weak wind-textured windswell over the reef: short crumbly lines that stand up briefly and reform, plenty of surface chop from the 18g22kt N cross-shore. Not closeouts in the classic sense, just gutless - no green wall with a shoulder running off the lip in any of the 3 detail frames or 6 sheet frames. Scanned the takeoff zone, both shoulders and the inside channel in every detail frame and both crowd frames: no bodies anywhere in the water, no boards, no paddling lines. Confident 0 out. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

08:56 sunrise run. Morning sun is low from the right and lights the cliff and buildings warm, but the water itself is fully readable this run - no blowout, unlike the 18:05 run. The bay is effectively flat: uniform wind ripple with a couple of soft knee-high reforms crossing the inside near the rocks and a wash on the point. No swell line stands up anywhere in the 3 detail frames. Scanned the whole open bay, the corner by the rocks and the shorebreak in every detail and crowd frame: nobody in the water at all. 0 out, and given how flat it is that is unsurprising rather than a missed-opportunity empty lineup. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

08:56 sunrise run. No images this run - the HLS stream at hls.cdn-surfline.com/ireland/pt-ribeiradeilhas/playlist.m3u8 returned 404 Not Found and ffmpeg failed, so collect.py wrote no sheet, crowd or detail crop. No vision read is possible: surfers and people both null. This is a dead cam, NOT an empty lineup - and it matters, because Ribeira is the one spot rated FAIR this run with the N wind blowing offshore there, so it is the spot most likely to have people on it. Metrics still collected normally

08:56 sunrise run, wide distant cam so all counts approximate. Cam is clean and bright with no glare this morning. Wave is small and wind-chopped: a broad band of whitewater rolling in across the sand with a slightly better peak on the bank near the headland, nothing with a proper wall. In the water there is a loose cluster of dark specks sitting outside the whitewater in the right-hand third of the frame - roughly 5 at the higher of the two crowd frames, plus one or two closer in near the rocks in the detail frames. At this range a surfer and a bodyboarder are indistinguishable, so ~5 out is approximate. On land: a group of about 5 in pink jerseys standing together on the sand by the rocks (looks like a surf-school or lifeguard group) plus 4-5 scattered sitting figures along the waterline, so roughly 10 on the sand - approximate. Beach is near-empty for the hour

18:05 sunset run. Low sun from the left but the Norte frame stays legible - water is dark blue, no blowout. Wave is a weak wind-textured shorebreak: small crumbly reforming lines close in, nothing standing up outside, no green wall in any of the 3 detail frames. Scanned takeoff zone, shoulder and inside channel in every detail and crowd frame: one dark body in the water mid-frame at +0s on the crowd crop, and a second reddish figure with what looks like a board in the shorebreak at +37s; the +25s detail frame shows an orange/red figure prone in the wash. Calling 2 in the water, and they read as bodyboarders/swimmers in the shorebreak rather than surfers on a wave. Two or three people on the promenade at the bottom edge of the sheet frames but the cam is framed on the water, so land count not applicable

18:05 sunset run. Low sun sits directly in the left third of the Sul frame and blows it to pure white - that is exactly where the beach and takeoff zone are. The readable right-hand half of the bay (open water, the point and the outer rock) is empty across all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames, but the part of the water that matters is unreadable, so recording surfers as null rather than claiming an empty lineup. Wave read from the legible half: effectively flat - uniform wind ripple, the only whitewater is a wash on the rocks under the point and a boil over the outer rock, no swell line standing up. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

18:05 sunset run. Cam is back up after last run's 404, but the detail and crowd crops are aimed too high this run - both are filled with open horizon and a lamp post, with the lineup off the bottom of the frame, so the magnified crops are useless for counting. On the wide contact sheet the surf zone sits under the sun glare track and I cannot resolve boards from bathers there, so surfers = null rather than a guess. There is one small dark object bottom-left of the +0s crowd frame that could be a surfer but I will not count it. Wave read from the sheet: small clean waist-high lines coming in with the strong N offshore holding them up - the best-looking water of the four spots. Land is countable and busy: people spread the full width of the sand, a line of them along the waterline and more on the promenade rail - roughly 50, approximate

18:05 sunset run, wide distant cam so all counts approximate. The camera looks straight into the setting sun and the entire surf zone is blown to white in all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames - the break line is not readable at all. Several figures stand at the waterline in the wash but nobody is resolvable seaward of the whitewater, and at this range a bodyboarder and a bather look identical, so surfers = null. Not an empty lineup - a glared-out cam. Wave read is limited to the darker left corner by the headland, where the wash on the rocks and a broad band of whitewater along the sand suggests the usual weak wind-blown shorebreak. Land is the readable half: still a busy end-of-August beach with umbrellas, sunbathers and walkers across the sand - roughly 60, approximate

15:32 afternoon run, bright sun, no glare on the water, fully legible. Tide well up towards the 16:47 high so the reef is covered; the whole visible bay is dark blue wind chop with no organised line standing up anywhere. The only breaking water in any frame is a short crumbly line on the far right near the shore rocks, and it is foam only - no green wall behind it in either crowd frame. Scanned takeoff zone, right-hand shoulder and inside channel across all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames: no boards, no bodies, no paddle trails. Calling 0 out. Two or three people on the promenade at the bottom edge of the sheet frames, but the cam is framed on the water so land count not applicable

afternoon sun with a warm haze on the image but the bay is readable, no glare blocking the water. Effectively flat: across all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames the only white water is a thin wash on the rocks under the point/hotel and a small boil over the outer rock. The open bay is uniform wind ripple with no swell line standing up at all. No bodies anywhere in the water in any frame. Calling 0 out. Sunbathers visible on the terraces by the point, but the cam is framed on the water so land count not applicable

NO IMAGES THIS RUN - the Surfline HLS playlist for pt-ribeiradeilhas returned 404 and ffmpeg could not open the stream, so no clip, no sheet, no crowd crop, no detail crop. Cam down, not an empty lineup. Forecast data collected normally (POOR_TO_FAIR 0.6-0.9m, 15g17kt NNW cross-shore, best rated of the four)

wide distant cam so all counts here are approximate. Bright afternoon sun, water readable near shore. Wave is a weak wind-blown shorebreak: a broad band of whitewater right along the sand with nothing standing up outside it, and the whole line goes white at once across successive frames - closed out and unrideable. In the water I can see roughly half a dozen figures but every one of them is standing waist-deep in the wash at the shoreline; no boards, no one paddling, nobody seaward of the break in any of the 3 detail frames or 2 crowd frames. At this range a bodyboarder and a bather are identical, and since none of these figures is beyond the whitewater I will not claim a surfer count - recording surfers as null rather than guessing. Land is the story: a packed August Sunday beach, umbrella line running the full width of the sand plus walkers and a group at the waterline - roughly 100 people, approximate

11:31 lunch run, bright sun but no glare on the water, fully legible. Deep low-tide look: outer reef and inside slabs dry, a wide sand lagoon in the middle. Waves are thin crumbly lines breaking way out on the outer reef and reforming as ankle wash on the inside - the +25s and +50s detail frames show foam lines with no green wall standing up behind them, so it is not a closeout, it is simply too shallow and too weak to ride. Scanned takeoff zone, reef shoulder and inside channel in all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames: no boards, no bodies in the surf. Calling 0 out. Two people wading in the lagoon and a handful of walkers on the promenade, but the cam is framed on the water so land count not applicable

sun high and slightly hazy but the bay is readable, no glare. Effectively flat - across all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames the only white water is a thin wash breaking on the rocks under the point/hotel; the open bay shows low unbroken swell lines that never stand up. No bodies anywhere in the water. Calling 0 out. Sunbathers visible on the sand by the point, but the cam is framed on the water so land count not applicable

CAM IS BACK UP after being down for three runs - first vision pass here since 28 Aug. Bright, clear, water readable. Low tide with the reef shelf mostly dry; the rideable wave is well outside on the point, peeling right in clean small walls (detail +0s shows an unbroken green face ahead of the foam, so peeling not closing out), just small and wind-textured by the 13kt NNW cross-shore. Counted from both crowd frames, taking the higher: a cluster of 3 sitting out the back plus 2 further inside on the +0s frame, and 6 spread along the point on the +37s frame with 2 more paddling wide - reconciling across frames gives 8 out. Well under the 21 average for this slot. On land: roughly 22 - about a dozen on the promenade and reef edge, a few under umbrellas at the top of the sand, 4-5 sunbathers scattered on the beach and a couple of walkers, approximate

wide distant cam so all counts here are approximate. Sun is high, no glare, water readable. Wave is a fat shorebreak dumping straight onto the sand across most of the beach - successive frames show the whole line going white at once on the inside, a genuine closeout - with only a small workable corner tucked in by the rocks at the north end. Detail +25s and +50s show 4-5 dark shapes in the water at the south end near the flag; at this range a bodyboarder and a swimmer look identical, so ~4 in the water and most of them are probably bathers, not surfers. Beach is busy for the conditions: counted roughly 32 people across the crowd frames - a group of 8-10 standing at the waterline mid-beach, scattered sunbathers and umbrellas, a few by the lifeguard stand, approximate

07:39 sunrise run, full daylight, overcast so no glare - water fully legible. Tide draining to the 10:33 low and the outer reef is well exposed; small NNW wind-chopped lines break over the reef and reform on the inside, one short green shoulder on the left in the detail +50s frame so it is not all closeout, but nothing worth paddling for. Scanned takeoff zone, reef shoulder and inside channel in all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames: no bodies. Calling 0 out. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

flat to near-flat. Overcast, hazy but readable, no glare. Across all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames the bay shows only a thin band of wash running off the point rocks and low unbroken swell lines that never stand up - there is no breaking wave in the bay at all. No bodies anywhere in the water. Calling 0 out. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

CAM DOWN for the third run running - the Surfline HLS stream (pt-ribeiradeilhascloseup) returned 404 again and collect.py wrote no sheet, crowd or detail image, so there was no vision pass for this spot. Surfline forecast data (FAIR, 0.3-0.6m, 9g12kt NNW cross-shore) still collected. Not countable - null, not 0

overcast, no glare, water readable but the cam is wide and distant so this is approximate. Wave is a small crumbly shorebreak dumping close to the sand, with one short green peeling section in the detail +25s frame; no outside bank working. One dark shape sits in the shorebreak in the detail +25s frame and again further along in +50s - most likely a single bodyboarder or swimmer, so ~1 out, approximate, could be 0. Beach essentially deserted: 1-2 people at the waterline plus a large flock of gulls on the sand which are birds, not people - calling 2 on land, approximate

sunset run, still full daylight and the water is fully legible - no glare on this cam. Surface is completely wind-textured by the NNW 11g14kt onshore; several overlapping broken lines reform across the inside and the outer reef section throws a short section on the right of frame, but there is no clean green wall anywhere in the 3 detail frames. Scanned takeoff zone, shoulder and channel in all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames: nothing in the water. Calling 0 out. Cam is framed on the water so land count not applicable

low sun sits directly down the cam axis and blows out the left/north half of the water with glitter; the right half around the point is clean and readable. Almost nothing breaking - a thin wash on the point rocks and small unbroken lines that do not stand up. Scanned all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames: no bodies resolve in the readable half or in the shorebreak by the rocks. Calling 0 out, with the caveat that the glare band on the north half could hide a body. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

CAM DOWN for the second run running - the Surfline HLS stream (pt-ribeiradeilhascloseup) returned 404 and collect.py wrote no sheet, crowd or detail image, so there was no vision pass for this spot. Surfline forecast data (FAIR, 0.6-0.9m, 11g14kt NNW cross-shore) still collected. Not countable - null, not 0

golden hour, sun low and straight down the cam axis: the entire water surface from the shorebreak out is a sheet of blown-out glitter in every frame. Surfers in the lineup are genuinely not resolvable - reporting null, not 0. A few dark silhouettes stand at the waterline in the shorebreak but those are waders, not surfers, and I am not counting them as being out. Wave read from the foam band only: a wide continuous wind-blown shorebreak dumping onto the sand, 32% whitewater, no rideable outside bank. Beach still busy at sunset though thinner than the 15:32 run - roughly 70 people on the sand across both crowd frames, approximate

bright afternoon light, water fully legible, no glare problem. Onshore NNW 11g13kt has the surface completely wind-textured - three or four overlapping broken lines reforming across the inside, no clean green wall anywhere in the 3 detail frames. Scanned takeoff zone, shoulder and channel in all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames: nothing in the water. Calling 0 out. Two people on the promenade at +12s in the sheet, but cam is framed on the water so land count not applicable

clean read, no glare. Thin ragged wind lines running toward the point, crumbling early with no real face behind them - weaker than at 11:30. Scanned all 3 detail frames plus both crowd frames: no bodies resolve anywhere in the lineup or the shorebreak by the rocks. Calling 0 out. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

CAM DOWN - the Surfline HLS stream returned 404 and collect.py wrote no sheet, crowd or detail image, so there was no vision pass for this spot at all. Surfline forecast data (FAIR, 0.6-0.9m, 11g13kt NNW cross-shore) still collected. Not countable - null, not 0

approx - cam is wide and distant so bodies are only a few pixels, but the frame is bright and the waterline is clear. Wind-blown shorebreak dumping onto the sand in a wide continuous foam band, no rideable outside bank. Across the 3 detail frames and both crowd frames only two dark specks sit outside the foam (both in the +0s crowd frame, one reappears at +37s); a handful more are waders standing in knee-deep whitewater and are not counted. Reporting 2 as approximate. Beach itself is packed - dozens of umbrellas and sunbathers end to end, ~150 on the sand, approximate

bright midday light, water fully legible. Dead low tide - the reef shelf is dry across most of the frame and the inside is a shallow flat lagoon. Surf is breaking way out on the outer reef in three or four overlapping lines that reform into weak whitewater, no real green wall. Scanned takeoff zone, shoulder and channel in all 3 detail frames plus both crowd frames: one dark shape in crowd frame 1 that does not reappear in frame 2 and reads as a rock uncovering, no confirmed surfer. Calling 0 out. A few people walking the exposed reef shelf top-right, but cam is framed on the water so land count not applicable

clean read, no glare. Best-looking water of the four - long unbroken swell lines with green faces and a soft shoulder peeling toward the point, definitely not closeouts, just small. 2 dark specks resolve in crowd frame 1 (one mid-lineup, one near the shorebreak by the rocks) and one rider is visible on a wave in detail frame 2; reporting 2 as the higher count. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

busiest by far. Counted the speck line along the outer lineup in both crowd frames - ~20 in frame 1 and ~20 again in frame 2, so 20 is a solid count rather than an estimate, in line with the 22 average for this slot. Waves peeling with workable walls, light cross-shore texture. Beach is packed with summer crowd - umbrellas, tents and sunbathers across the sand and the rock shelf, ~70 people on land, approximate

approx - cam is wide and distant so bodies are only a few pixels, but the frame is bright and the waterline is clear. Swell is dumping straight onto the sand as a heavy shorebreak with a wide foam band and no rideable outside bank at this tide. Scanned all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames: only waders standing in knee-deep foam, nobody sitting outside on a board. Reporting 0 out as approximate. Land is busy with beachgoers, ~60, approximate

dawn light, dim but water legible - surface texture resolves clearly in the detail crop. Scanned takeoff zone, shoulder and inside across all 3 detail frames plus both crowd frames: nobody in the water. Surface crossed-up with several short-period lines overlapping, whitewater reforming across the flats, few unbroken faces. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

backlit dawn but water legible. Cleanest lines of the three readable spots - long soft unbroken swell lines rolling in, not closeouts, but weak and mostly only breaking near the rocks on the point. Detail crop checked frame by frame, nobody out. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

NO CAM THIS RUN - the Surfline HLS playlist returned 404 (pt-ribeiradeilhascloseup), so collect.py wrote no sheet, crowd or detail images. Nothing was seen; null is a missing read, not an empty lineup. Metrics only for this spot

approx - sun already up and the frame is bright and clear, but the cam is wide and distant so bodies are only a few pixels. 2 dark specks resolve in the water right of the lifeguard chair in both crowd frames and in detail frames 1 and 3; reporting 2 as approximate, could be one or two more. On land: 2 surfers walking down the sand carrying boards (detail frames 2 and 3) plus 1 figure sitting near the rocks - ~3, approximate

detail crop legible (low late sun but no glare on this framing). Scanned takeoff zone, shoulder and inside across all 3 detail frames plus both crowd frames - nobody in the water. Surface is crossed-up, foam stacked on foam from the 13g16kt NNW cross-shore, very few unbroken faces. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

water clearly legible. Better shape than Norte - long unbroken green walls with a running shoulder at +0s and +50s, not closeouts - but fat and wind-textured. Detail crop checked frame by frame, nobody out. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

approx - low sun glare on the outer lineup. 2 resolved in detail frame 1 (one riding, one sitting outside), 1 riding in frame 3; crowd crops show 2-3 specks in the same zone. Reporting 3, could be more hidden in the glare. Land count approximate, ~45 across sand and path, beach busy with umbrellas

sun setting straight down the beach - the entire lineup is a sheet of glare and the water is unreadable, so surfers is null not 0. Figures that do resolve are all at the waterline or on the sand. Where visible the surf is whitewater-heavy (ww 34%). ~35 on the sand, approximate

detail and crowd crops both legible, bright afternoon sun, no glare. Scanned takeoff zone, shoulder and inside on every frame - nobody in the water. Waves are NOT closeouts: clean green faces with a running shoulder at +0s and +50s, just chopped by the 10-12kt NW onshore. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

water heavily sanded and full of foam, reforming mush over the inside bank with no defined peak; detail crop checked frame by frame, nobody out. Water legible, so 0 rather than null. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

approx - ~4 visible in crowd frame 1, ~8 spread along the outer lineup in frame 2 (+37s); reporting the higher. Far quieter than the ~22 at the 11:31 run, the surf school has gone. Land count approximate, ~70 across sand and the path, beach very busy

approx - wide distant cam but people on the sand resolve clearly, so water is readable: it is a wall of whitewater and dumping closeout shorebreak end to end, nobody in the surf. ~45 on the sand, approximate
CORRECTED: original read of 'wide closeouts, 0 out' was wrong - waves were peeling with a defined shoulder and surfers were present. True count unknown, so NULL rather than a guess.

counted 6 heads in frame 1 and 6 in frame 2 including one up and riding on the outer bank; higher-confidence total 7. Glassy, one defined peak outside. Cam framed on the water so land count not applicable

approx - busiest of the four. Roughly 17 in a tight surf-school cluster on the inside by the point plus ~5 scattered out the back on the lined-up walls. Land count approximate, ~60 across sand and promenade
approx - wide distant cam but water readable, nobody in the surf; full closeouts end to end and a red flag flying. ~25 people on the sand, approximate
dawn light, water clearly legible in both crowd frames; glassy 3kt offshore with peeling lines at the point - lineup completely empty
post-sunset dusk but water still legible; low tide has the reef dry and swell reforming as whitewater across the flat - lineup empty
crumbly crossed-up lines with onshore texture, no clean shoulder; empty
cleanest of the four - occasional workable left through the inside; 2 in the water (higher of the two frames), ~5 on the sand and promenade
wide distant cam plus dusk haze at 20:19 - could not resolve anyone in the whitewater, so no surfer count; ~8 on the sand, approximate
several shifting peaks but all crossed-up and closing out onto the bar; lineup empty
bumpy chop dragging over the reef shelf, no rideable shoulder; empty
wall-to-wall whitewater, no lines; ~14 walkers on sand and promenade, nobody in the water
heavy sun glare straight down the lineup at 18:04 - could not resolve anyone in the water, so no surfer count; ~20 on the sand, approximate (wide cam)
closeouts to the sand, no shoulders, empty
chop over the reef shelf, no shape, empty
full whitewater field, no lines; promenade filling with evening walkers, water empty
one closeout band; beach emptying as the sun drops, water empty; wide cam so land count approximate
closeouts to the sand, no shoulders, empty
chop over the reef shelf, no shape, empty
full whitewater field, messiest ww reading yet (31.7%); 3 walking the sand, water empty
one closeout band, tide dropping; ~12 on the sand, water empty; wide cam so land count approximate
closeout lines to the sand, no shoulders, empty
chop washing over the reef shelf, no shape, empty
messiest of the four; 2 on the promenade, nobody in the water
one closeout band the length of the beach; busy sand, empty water; wide cam so land count approximate
